commentary: Sweden's unemployment at 8.7% in 2025 — its highest since 2021 — provides the macroeconomic backdrop against which the April 2026 employer contribution cut's documented failure (HD10444: profit capture rather than hiring) is particularly damaging. The GDP contraction in 2023 (-0.2%) followed by weak 2024 recovery (0.82%) means Sweden has limited fiscal room for experiments that fail to achieve their stated objectives. The Region Stockholm eating disorder care access improvement from 38% (2022) to 94% (2025) is the most quantifiable evidence in this batch — directly falsifying the Finance Minister's September 2025 parliamentary statement, as validated by the Stockholm District Court ruling of April 1, 2026.
